_comment: Production balancing (Homestead's own values, not taken from the original). Times in game seconds. Workshop inputs/outputs must match the building's request/offer piles in data/buildings. Mines eat one unit of whatever food their input piles hold per ore.

smiths._comment: One product per cycle: tools somebody waits for first, otherwise the product with the fewest units around while below keepInStock; with everything in stock the smith rests.

tools._comment: Tool a carrier must take to become the trade (game knowledge, as in JSettlers' EMovableType). BLADE is the digger's shovel.

storage._comment: Units per storehouse pile; a storehouse has six piles, each holding one material at a time. A full storehouse takes nothing more: goods then wait at the producers.
storage._materialsComment: What carriers bring to storehouses. Everything else stays at its producer (output pile of 8; the producer waits when it is full) and is fetched from there when needed.

housing._comment: Carriers a finished living house sends out through its door, one every intervalSeconds. Houses that come with a loaded map do not (the map lists its settlers itself).

resources._comment: Mountains and waters: a field of the original maps holds an amount of 0-15 (mostly 8). orePerAmount/fishPerAmount = units per amount step, so a mine's stock scales with it. regenerateSeconds: a depleted field regains one step this often (0 = never).
